summary:
OUTPOST COMMANDER is an interactive, web-based Mars and Moon exploration simulator that transforms space science into an engaging STEM learning experience. We developed a planetary exploration and outpost-management game where players take on the role of mission commanders. They operate rovers, collect resources such as water ice and regolith, manage energy and life-support systems, monitor crew health, and respond to environmental challenges. The simulator introduces the interconnected systems and critical decisions required to sustain human exploration beyond Earth. It also features timed educational facts about Mars and the Moon, helping players learn while completing missions.

OUTPOST COMMANDER addresses the challenge by making planetary exploration concepts accessible through interactive simulation rather than passive learning. It demonstrates how engineering, scientific knowledge and resource management work together in space missions. The project is important because it encourages curiosity, critical thinking and interest in STEM, inspiring young people in Rwanda, across Africa and worldwide to imagine themselves contributing to humanity's future in space.
details:
PROJECT ABACAMANZAOUTPOST COMMANDER

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: Interactive Mars & Moon Exploration Simulator

Location: Kigali, Rwanda
Challenge: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
Target audience: Young learners aged 7–12, with potential to engage older students and educators
Platform: Browser-based web application

1. Project Overview

OUTPOST COMMANDER is an interactive planetary exploration and space-outpost management simulator developed by Project ABACAMANZA in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

The challenge highlights an important problem in space education: young learners often discover space through videos, posters and general scientific facts, but rarely experience the engineering decisions and competing demands that determine whether a real planetary mission succeeds.

We wanted to address this gap by creating an experience in which students become mission commanders rather than passive observers.

In OUTPOST COMMANDER, players explore Mars and the Moon, operate planetary rovers, collect resources, manage an outpost, monitor crew health and interact with interconnected engineering systems. They encounter challenges involving energy, oxygen, water, life support, radiation protection and environmental conditions.

Our central idea is to make the challenges of living beyond Earth understandable through exploration, interaction and decision-making.

OUTPOST COMMANDER is not just about reaching another planet. It is about understanding what it takes to stay there.

2. The Problem We Are Addressing

Establishing a sustained human presence on the Moon or Mars involves much more than transporting astronauts to another world. A successful mission requires reliable energy, life-support systems, food production, radiation protection, water management and communication.

These systems compete for limited resources.

For example:

  • Energy used to heat an outpost may not be available for other operations.
  • Maintaining oxygen and removing carbon dioxide are essential for crew survival.
  • Radiation protection becomes particularly important during periods of increased solar activity.
  • Water ice is a valuable resource because water supports several essential mission needs.
  • Food production requires resources, energy and functioning environmental systems.

These engineering relationships are difficult to communicate through traditional educational materials alone.

Our project addresses this educational gap by introducing planetary exploration and outpost operations through an interactive simulator.

3. Our Solution: How OUTPOST COMMANDER Works

Players become mission commanders responsible for exploring and operating a planetary outpost on Mars or the Moon.

The experience combines several connected gameplay areas.

A. Planetary Exploration and Rover Operations

Players explore planetary terrain using a six-wheel rover. They can navigate the environment, use radar scanning, change camera perspectives and search for useful resources.

The rover experience introduces the importance of mobility, exploration and identifying resources in unfamiliar environments.

B. Resource Collection

Players can collect resources such as water ice and regolith.

This introduces the concept of using locally available planetary materials rather than depending entirely on supplies transported from Earth.

C. Outpost Management

Players interact with simulated systems needed to sustain a human presence beyond Earth, including:

  • Power generation and battery reserves.
  • Oxygen production.
  • Carbon dioxide removal.
  • Life-support systems.
  • Radiation protection.
  • Hydroponics and food production.
  • Water management.
  • Crew health monitoring.

These features introduce the different engineering systems that must work together to support a planetary outpost.

D. Energy Management

Energy is one of the most important considerations in planetary operations.

The simulator introduces power-generation concepts, including solar power, nuclear power generation and battery storage.

Players interact with power-management systems and explore how energy supports different outpost operations.

E. Environmental Challenges

The project introduces environmental conditions associated with planetary exploration, including dust storms, extreme temperatures and solar particle events.

These challenges help learners understand why planetary environments require specialized equipment, preparation and protection.

F. Educational Discoveries

The Did You Know? feature introduces educational facts about Mars and the Moon approximately every two minutes during gameplay.

The application also includes educational sections such as NASA 3D Planetary Observatory, NASA Intel and NASA Tech Manual.

These features connect the interactive experience with further scientific exploration.

4. How Our Project Responds to NASA's Challenge

NASA's challenge specifically asks participants to create an interactive experience where children understand the competing demands involved in operating a lunar or Martian outpost.

OUTPOST COMMANDER responds through the following areas:

NASA challenge requirement

OUTPOST COMMANDER response

Lunar or Martian outpost

Players explore both Mars and the Moon

Life support

Oxygen production and CO₂ removal systems

Power management

Solar power, nuclear generation and battery reserves

Radiation protection

Outpost radiation-protection systems and solar-event challenges

Food production

Hydroponics systems

Resource management

Water ice and regolith collection

Environmental conditions

Dust storms and extreme temperatures

Interactive learning

Playable exploration and management interfaces

Educational accessibility

Browser-based experience and Did You Know? facts

The project brings these elements together to introduce the complexity of planetary missions in a format designed to be engaging for young learners.

The key educational principle is that a planetary outpost is an interconnected system: decisions about one part of the mission can affect the others.

5. Our Unique Approach and Creativity

Our uniqueness lies in combining planetary exploration with the responsibilities of operating a space outpost.

Many educational experiences focus on explaining what Mars or the Moon looks like. OUTPOST COMMANDER goes further by introducing what astronauts and mission planners must consider when exploring and living in these environments.

Our approach has several distinguishing features:

Two planetary environments: Players can explore both Mars and the Moon within one experience.

Exploration combined with engineering: Rover operations and resource collection are connected to the wider experience of managing a planetary outpost.

Multiple connected systems: The simulator introduces power, life support, oxygen, radiation protection, hydroponics and crew health together rather than treating them as unrelated topics.

Learning during gameplay: The Did You Know? feature introduces scientific facts while players are completing their missions.

A broader mission experience: Instead of focusing on a single activity, the application introduces exploration, resource discovery, outpost operations and crew protection.

Our goal is to make complex space-related concepts understandable without removing the excitement of exploration.

6. How Players Learn

OUTPOST COMMANDER uses experiential learning: students learn by interacting with a simulated mission, making decisions and observing what happens.

For example, a player can explore a planetary environment, collect resources, examine the outpost's energy systems and investigate how power supports life-support operations.

They can then connect these experiences with scientific explanations through the educational features.

The experience encourages:

  • Critical thinking.
  • Systems thinking.
  • Resource-management awareness.
  • Scientific curiosity.
  • Engineering problem-solving.
  • Independent exploration.

For the intended audience of ages 7–12, the visual and interactive format helps introduce concepts that might otherwise feel too technical or abstract.

7. NASA Scientific Resources

Scientific credibility is important when teaching young people about real planetary exploration.

We identified the following NASA resources as relevant references and potential sources for strengthening the simulator's scientific foundation.

NASA APIs

https://api.nasa.gov/

NASA's API portal provides access to scientific information and datasets that developers can use in educational applications.

NASA 3D Mars Model

https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/gltf_embed/2372/

A planetary visualization that supports exploration of Mars.

NASA 3D Moon Model

https://solarsystem.nasa.gov/gltf_embed/2366/

A three-dimensional Moon visualization that supports planetary learning.

NASA Open Data Portal

https://data.nasa.gov/

NASA's collection of publicly available datasets.

NASA Science

https://science.nasa.gov/

NASA's scientific information about planetary environments, missions and discoveries.

Additional datasets relevant to the challenge

NASA DONKI – Space Weather Database:
https://kauai.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/

Can support future features involving real solar events and space-weather information.

NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR):
https://osdr.nasa.gov/

Provides research data relevant to astronaut health and biological responses to spaceflight.

These resources offer opportunities to strengthen the scientific grounding of the project. We distinguish between resources currently presented or used in the application and datasets identified for potential future integration. We do not describe static information as live data.

8. Development Tools and Technology

OUTPOST COMMANDER was developed as a browser-based web application with the support of AI-assisted development tools.

Lovable: Supported the development and refinement of the application and its interface.

Google AI Studio: Supported the AI-assisted development process.

The application brings together interactive planetary environments, rover operations, resource-management interfaces and educational content in a web-based experience.

Its browser-based design reduces the need for specialized physical equipment and makes the experience easier to access.

9. Intended Impact

Our main objective is to make planetary science and aerospace engineering more engaging and accessible to young learners.

We believe children should have opportunities to explore not only the discoveries of space exploration but also the engineering, planning and scientific reasoning behind them.

Through OUTPOST COMMANDER, we aim to:

  1. Make planetary science more interactive and understandable.
  2. Encourage young learners to explore STEM subjects.
  3. Introduce the engineering challenges of human exploration beyond Earth.
  4. Develop curiosity, problem-solving and systems-thinking skills.
  5. Inspire students in Rwanda, across Africa and worldwide to imagine themselves contributing to future space exploration.

We want students to understand that space exploration is not only about astronauts travelling to distant worlds. It is also about the scientists, engineers, programmers and problem-solvers who make those missions possible.


Live application:
https://aerospace-stem.lovable.app/

11. Conclusion

OUTPOST COMMANDER was created around one important question:

What does it really take to keep humans alive and operating on another world?

Our response is an interactive experience that introduces young learners to planetary exploration, resource collection, energy management, life support and the connected systems behind a successful space mission.

By bringing these concepts into one accessible digital environment, Project ABACAMANZA aims to help children move beyond simply learning facts about space and begin understanding the decisions that make space exploration possible.

We want to turn curiosity about space into an interest in science, engineering and innovation.

Explore beyond Earth. Understand the mission. Inspire the next generation.
